method: Actual Windows app screenshots and accessibility states reviewed through Computer Use. Computer Use screenshot pixels were not decoded, saved or measured programmatically.

cases.positionLimit: The accessible seek retained its requested normalized value until the subtitle refresh reconciled the timer. The elapsed text stayed at five seconds and the top frame-marker pattern stayed identical. This does not qualify exact GUI slider-value conservation or absolute PTS; the native marker/no-audio-time checks are the quantitative conservation evidence.

cases.inputLimit: The first indexed subtitle-button click reported unavailable coordinate geometry. A refreshed screenshot and one retry opened the panel. Later accessibility observations lagged a Qt frame; fresh observations confirmed the final states.
cases.uiFollowUp: A transient Next frame OSD appeared immediately after ASS loading, although the paused picture-marker pattern remained identical. The cause is not yet qualified; this is not accepted as correct user feedback.

A transient Next frame OSD reappeared on the explicit external Finnish/English changes with no step key sent; the visible marker remained the same. This independently confirms the feedback follow-up observed in the ASS run.

limits: The SubRip first accessible seek reconciles its normalized slider value after track loading. No exact GUI slider-value or absolute seek-PTS acceptance is claimed.
Visible frame-marker patterns are manual desktop observations; native snapshot marker pixels separately qualify actual frame conservation.
The transient Next frame message on subtitle refresh is a reproduced UI-feedback follow-up, not accepted correct behavior.
No whole subtitle, cold-initial-caption, complete layout, physical audibility, Windows10, DPI or full-beta acceptance.
